About Bask Health
 Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.
 Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.
 We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.
 Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.
 About the Role
 We're looking for a Frontend Engineering Intern to join Bask Health's engineering team and gain hands-on experience building modern web applications.
 This internship is designed for students, recent graduates, and aspiring software engineers who want to strengthen their frontend development skills while contributing to real product features. You'll work alongside experienced engineers, designers, and product managers to help build and improve the interfaces that power Bask's telehealth platform.
 You'll contribute to frontend components, responsive layouts, forms, application workflows, and user interface improvements. Your projects may involve merchant dashboards, patient-facing experiences, storefronts, or internal applications used by Bask's teams.
 You'll gain practical experience with technologies such as React, Next.js, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS while learning how professional engineering teams plan, develop, test, review, and deploy software.
 This is a hands-on engineering internship, not an observational program. You'll write code, participate in development discussions, receive feedback through code reviews, and contribute to features that may be used in production.
 We're looking for someone who enjoys programming, is eager to learn, and takes initiative when solving problems. You don't need previous professional experience, but you should have a basic understanding of frontend development and be able to demonstrate your interest through coursework, personal projects, or other hands-on experience.
 What You'll Do
 
• Assist with developing frontend features across Bask Health's web applications. 
• Work with experienced engineers to implement user interface components and application functionality. 
• Write frontend code using JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and Next.js. 
• Help build responsive interfaces using HTML, CSS, and modern frontend development techniques. 
• Develop reusable components for merchant-facing and internal applications. 
• Assist with implementing forms, navigation elements, buttons, modals, and other interactive components. 
• Translate design specifications and Figma files into working frontend interfaces. 
• Support improvements to merchant dashboards, storefronts, and patient-facing experiences. 
• Help connect frontend components to backend APIs and application data. 
• Assist with implementing basic application state and interactive functionality. 
• Learn how to handle user input, validation, and error messages. 
• Help identify and resolve frontend bugs and layout issues. 
• Test interfaces across different browsers and screen sizes. 
• Support accessibility and responsive design improvements. 
• Collaborate with designers to improve visual consistency and usability. 
• Learn and apply frontend coding standards and development best practices. 
• Write clean, readable, and maintainable code. 
• Assist with writing unit tests and checking frontend functionality. 
• Participate in code reviews and apply feedback from experienced engineers. 
• Use Git and established development workflows to manage code changes. 
• Help document reusable components and implementation details. 
• Participate in engineering discussions and team collaboration. 
• Learn how frontend applications interact with backend services. 
• Assist with improving application performance and loading behavior. 
• Explore new frontend technologies and development techniques when relevant. 
• Use AI-assisted development tools while reviewing and understanding generated code. 
• Complete assigned development tasks with guidance and gradually take on more responsibility.

Requirements
 
• Currently studying computer science, software engineering, web development, or a related field, or developing equivalent skills through bootcamps or independent learning. 
• Basic knowledge of JavaScript. 
• Familiarity with HTML and CSS. 
• Foundational understanding of how websites and web applications work. 
• Basic experience with React or another frontend framework through coursework or personal projects. 
• Interest in learning TypeScript and modern frontend development tools. 
• Understanding of fundamental programming concepts. 
• Familiarity with responsive web design principles. 
• Basic understanding of reusable UI components. 
• Willingness to learn how frontend applications communicate with APIs. 
• Familiarity with Git or willingness to learn version control. 
• Ability to write organized and readable code. 
• Basic problem-solving and debugging skills. 
• Attention to detail when implementing frontend interfaces. 
• Interest in user interface development and user experience. 
• Willingness to learn software testing and quality assurance practices. 
• Ability to follow technical instructions and development guidelines. 
• Strong curiosity and willingness to explore unfamiliar technologies. 
• Ability to ask questions and seek guidance when needed. 
• Openness to constructive feedback and code reviews. 
• Good communication and collaboration skills. 
• Ability to manage assigned tasks and communicate progress. 
• Willingness to learn professional software development workflows. 
• Genuine interest in building useful web applications. 
• Comfort collaborating with a remote engineering team. Nice to Have
 
• Personal projects demonstrating frontend development skills. 
• Coursework or projects involving React. 
• Familiarity with TypeScript. 
• Experience building applications with Next.js. 
• Familiarity with Tailwind CSS or comparable styling frameworks. 
• Experience translating Figma designs into working interfaces. 
• Familiarity with responsive layouts using Flexbox and CSS Grid. 
• Experience building forms or interactive web components. 
• Basic understanding of REST APIs. 
• Familiarity with browser developer tools. 
• Experience using GitHub for personal or collaborative projects. 
• Exposure to component libraries or design systems. 
• Familiarity with frontend state management concepts. 
• Experience writing basic unit tests. 
• Exposure to accessibility and semantic HTML. 
• Experience building a personal portfolio website. 
• Contributions to open-source or collaborative development projects. 
• Interest in e-commerce, SaaS, or healthcare technology. 
• Familiarity with frontend deployment platforms or CI/CD workflows. 
• Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor or Claude Code.
fit_why: React/TypeScript/Node full-stack web experience matches frontend internship well

 We're looking for a Backend Engineering Intern to join Bask Health's engineering team and gain hands-on experience building software for our telehealth platform.

Introduction to the job
 
 ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
 
 The Customer Support (CS) organization is responsible for the installation, qualification, repair and maintenance of the ASML systems at customer sites and is responsible for the necessary transfer of know-how to the customer. Local Customer Support branches perform these tasks for the customers within the specific region.
 
 Roles and responsibilities
 
• Understand the basics of semiconductor manufacturing, especially the Lithography manufacturing process and the importance of ASML’s role.
 
• Learn about ASML’s products and Applications Engineering team's approach to enable next node developments with our customers.
 
• Obtain customer service skills in an tech industry environment
 
• Interns will typically be required to document and present their findings as well as making an end of summer presentation to the group about what they achieved during their internship.
 
 Potential projects may included:
 
• Optimize work processes using automation (scripts to generate engineering templates or download data from multiple sources for analysis)
 
• Use data analysis to solve complex problems (correlate machine parameters to customer product issues)
 
• Develop dashboards for efficient monitoring (use Spotfire to create and optimize real time monitoring dashboards to monitor system performance)
 
 Education and experience
 
• Minimum 60 hours completed (required) towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in an Engineering field.
 
• Preferred Majors: Physics, Optics, Electronics, Micro-electronics, Mechanical Engineering, Material Science Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering or IC manufacturing.
 
• Minimum 6 months experience with MATLAB, Python, or equivalent data analysis software.
 
• You are able to clearly communicate status and progress of a project to the engineering and management team
 
• You thrive in frequent collaboration with our teams and  customers
 
 Skills
 
 Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
 
 To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
 
• Can learn and apply new information or skills.
 
• Must be able to read and interpret data, information, and documents.
 
• Ability to complete assignments with attention to detail and high degree of accuracy.
 
• Proven ability to perform effectively in a demanding environment with changing workloads and deadlines.
 
• Result driven-demonstrate ownership and accountability.
 
• Identifies bottlenecks and drives improvements.
 
• Work independently or as part of a team and follow through on assignments with minimal supervision. 
 
• Demonstrate open, clear, concise and professional communication.
 
• Ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with manager, co-workers and customer.
 
• Work according to a strict set of procedures within the provided timelines.

 Inclusion and diversity 
 ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. We recognize that inclusion and diversity is a driving force in the success of our company.
 
 Need to know more about applying for a job at ASML? Read our frequently asked questions .
fit_why: Semiconductor lithography and Spotfire dashboards; little SWE overlap, Python data a plus

Please Note: 

 To provide the best candidate experience amidst our high application volumes, each candidate is limited to 10 applications across all open jobs within a 6-month period. 

 Advancing the World’s Technology Together 

 Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. Here, you’ll have an opportunity to be part of a global leader whose innovative designs are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and powering the future. 

 We believe innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We’re dedicated to empowering people to be their true selves. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities.

 What You'll Learn 

• Project Overview: Build a cost-model-guided auto-tuning framework for PyTorch and Triton kernels on Samsung’s compute-near-memory AI accelerator, and make it placement-aware, so that each kernel is tuned for where its data lives. You’ll connect it to torch.compile and measure the gains on LLM inference. 

• Skills You’ll Learn: 

• Performance optimisation for a cache-less, DMA-driven accelerator: search spaces, legality rules and cost models 

• PyTorch compiler internals (torch.compile, FX, Inductor autotuning) and Triton kernel compilation 

• Benchmarking and profiling LLM inference kernels (GEMM, attention) on simulators and hardware 

 What You’ll Do 

 Our ML Compiler team builds the software that runs PyTorch models on Samsung’s compute-near-memory AI accelerator: a PyTorch device and compiler backend, a Triton-based kernel compiler and an LLVM back end. We work closely with the runtime and hardware teams and with the PyTorch and Triton open-source communities. Over the summer you’ll own one piece of making ordinary PyTorch models fast on new memory-centric hardware, from research idea to merged, measured code. 

 Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose Headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy 

 Reports to: Director 

• Design a search space for Triton kernel configurations on the accelerator: tile sizes, launch-grid mapping, on-chip buffer budgets and load style. 

• Build legality rules with our compiler engineers that prune configurations that will not compile or will not fit in on-chip memory. 

• Develop a kernel cost model, calibrated against our simulator and profiler, that ranks candidates so only the most promising are benchmarked. 

• Build a reliable benchmarking harness and a persistent tuning cache, so that tuning cost stays practical. 

• Integrate the tuner with the torch.compile Inductor autotuning path and with Triton’s autotuner. 

• Extend tuning to data placement: tune kernels for a given tensor layout and export tuned costs that a placement pass can use. 

• Measure kernel-level and end-to-end LLM inference gains, and share results in weekly syncs and a final presentation. 

• Collaborate with PyTorch and Triton developers on upstream autotuning hooks, and hand off documented, tested code.

• Complete other responsibilities as assigned. 
 
 What You Bring 

• Pursuing a Masters or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or Electrical Engineering; PhD preferred. 

• Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining 

• Strong Python and C++, with experience writing or tuning Triton kernels or working with PyTorch compiler internals (torch.compile, FX, Inductor). 

• Grounding in compilers or performance engineering: IR and passes, cost models, roofline analysis and profiling. 

• Preferred: auto-tuning or auto-sharding experience (e.g. TVM/Ansor, the Halide autoscheduler, Kernel Tuner, Alpa, GSPMD), or search methods such as Bayesian optimisation or ILP. 

• Preferred: MLIR/LLVM back ends, scratchpad or near-memory architectures, LLM inference kernels, or publications or open-source PyTorch/Triton contributions.

• You’re inclusive, adapting your style to the situation and diverse global norms of our people. 

• An avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding. 

• You’re collaborative, building relationships, humbly offering support and openly welcoming approaches. 

• Innovative and creative, you proactively explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change. 
 
 #LI-AD1 
 What We Offer
 The pay range below is for all roles at this level across all US locations and functions. Pay within this range varies by work location and may also depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. 

 This is in addition to our diverse package of benefits centered around the wellbeing of our employees and their loved ones. In addition to the usual Medical/Dental/Vision, our inclusive rewards plan empowers our people to care for their whole selves. An investment in your future is an investment in ours. 

 Relocation Support Live 50+ miles away from your new office? No worries! We'll provide a stipend to help support your move. 
Housing Stipend Signing a lease on a new place for your summer internship? We'll help you pay your way with a monthly stipend. 
Give Back With a charitable giving match and frequent opportunities to get involved, we take an active role in supporting the community. 
Prioritize Emotional Wellness With on-demand apps and paid therapy sessions, you’ll have support no matter where you are. 
Stay Fit Eating well and being active are important parts of a healthy life. Our onsite Café and gym, plus virtual classes, make it easier. 
Embrace Flexibility Benefits are best when you have the space to use them. That’s why we facilitate a flexible environment so you can find the right balance for you. 

 Hourly Base Pay Rate
 $28 — $68 USD 

 Equal Opportunity Employment Policy  

 Samsung Semiconductor takes pride in being an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to fostering an environment where all individuals feel valued and empowered to excel, regardless of race, religion, color, age, disability, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, ancestry, genetic information, marital status, national origin, political affiliation, or veteran status.

 When selecting team members, we prioritize talent and qualities such as humility, kindness, and dedication. We extend comprehensive accommodations throughout our recruiting processes for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, neurodivergent individuals, or those requiring pregnancy-related support. All candidates scheduled for an interview will receive guidance on requesting accommodations.

 Advancing the World’s Technology Together 

 Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. Here, you’ll have an opportunity to be part of a global leader whose innovative designs are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and powering the future. 

 We believe innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We’re dedicated to empowering people to be their true selves. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities.

 What You’ll Learn 

• Project Overview: Build AgentSysBench, a benchmark suite and profiling toolchain that measures how AI agent frameworks (Claude Code, Aider, LangGraph) use server resources: host CPU, DRAM, GPU HBM and CXL memory. The results will guide memory system design for future AI data centers. 

• Skills You’ll Learn: 

• Profile system and microarchitecture performance with perf, eBPF, hardware PMUs and NVML/DCGM 

• Characterize memory hierarchies (HBM, DDR5, CXL) and build performance models 

• Benchmark LLM inference serving (vLLM/SGLang) on NVIDIA GPU servers 

 What You’ll Do 

 Our team researches the next-generation memory solutions for AI workloads, including HBM, DRAM, and CXL memory expansion. This summer, you'll work on servers with Samsung CXL memory expanders and NVIDIA GPUs. You'll see how agentic AI workloads stress memory systems and how those findings feed into future memory product architecture design. 

 Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy 

 Reports to:  Sr. Director 

• Build runtime adapters and a trace record/replay harness for AI agent frameworks 

• Develop micro-kernel and end-to-end agent workload benchmarks that stress CPU, memory, storage and accelerator subsystems 

• Profile agent workloads with perf, eBPF, PMUs and NVML/DCGM to break down per-turn latency and memory bandwidth usage 

• Measure host DDR5, GPU HBM and CXL.mem bandwidth and latency across Intel Xeon and/or AMD EPYC servers 

• Evaluate multi-agent KV-cache sharing and CXL memory expansion on Samsung CXL expanders 

• Build an initial memory tiering cost model (HBM/DDR5/CXL) for long-running MoE agent workloads 

• Present findings in weekly team meetings, then deliver a final report and presentation 

• Complete other responsibilities as assigned. 
 
 What You Bring 

• Pursuing PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field 

• Strong programming skills in Python and C/C++ in a Linux environment 

• Solid understanding of computer architecture (CPU caches, the memory hierarchy, NUMA) 

• Experience with performance profiling tools (perf, eBPF, VTune, or Nsight) 

• Preferred: hands-on experience with LLM serving frameworks (vLLM, SGLang) or GPU programming 

• Preferred: familiarity with HBM, CXL, or heterogeneous memory systems 

• Preferred: experience with AI agent frameworks or benchmark development 

• You’re inclusive, adapting your style to the situation and diverse global norms of our people. 

• An avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding. 

• You’re collaborative, building relationships, humbly offering support and openly welcoming approaches. 

• Innovative and creative, you proactively explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change.
